elements.element: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 11 states that the Agreement “shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York.”

elements.element: The state and federal courts located in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over disputes.
elements.evidence: Section 19 requires all defined Disputes to be “brought exclusively in the state or federal courts located in New York County, New York,” and each party submits to their exclusive jurisdiction and venue.

elements.element: The Agreement is governed by the laws of Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects New York law, not any accepted fallback governing law.

elements.element: Disputes are submitted to courts corresponding to the selected fallback law: Delaware courts, California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects state and federal courts in New York County, not Delaware or California courts or the courts of London.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the preferred New York governing-law and exclusive New York County court position. The fallback is assessed separately and is not met because neither its governing law nor its corresponding courts are selected. The substantive changes are limited to replacing Arizona law and mandatory arbitration with the preferred position, and unrelated severability terms remain intact. Drafting quality is reduced because Section 19 remains titled “Arbitration” even though arbitration has been removed, and the retained dispute-definition text is visibly incomplete or malformed around “whether directly or indirectly” and subsection “(b).”
